_doc: Paying a clock to hurry (ROADMAP §3.9, R86). WHY THIS SHAPE: §3.9 promised since M0 that every timer is skippable with an earned second currency. Measured before building, the premise was wrong twice — the Infirmary already ends its clock for money, priced by the hour, and the TWA pitch never mentions a skip — and the pacing problem it was designed for does not show up in a 180-day walk (longest stretch with nothing productive to do: zero hours). So R86 shipped the model the game already had rather than a second economy: the Infirmary's price, applied to every PURE WAIT. A pure wait is a clock whose outcome is SEALED when it starts — the vat, the resequencer, an egg and a settling chimera — so a rush can only ever buy time, never a different creature, and smoke proves it by decanting a rushed vat and a waited one and comparing the children. `tuning.base` is the flat call-out and `tuning.perHour` the rate on the hours left; splice/scars.js reads the same two numbers for treatment, so the Infirmary and a rush cannot drift apart. `kinds` carries the one line each rush says; `{name}` and `{price}` are filled in. Cooldowns, growth, rehab, jobs and the world's own clocks are NOT here on purpose — see splice/rush.js for the rule — and the registry that decides what is for sale is code, not this file, because 'a cooldown becomes buyable' is an engine decision with a §3.9 edit attached, not a content edit.

settle.label: Settling
settle.line: {name} was talked into settling early. ${price}, and a firm tone of voice.

vat.label: Gestation
vat.line: The vat was told to hurry. ${price}, and it complied with a noise nobody wants to hear twice.

resequencer.label: Resequencing
resequencer.line: The tank skipped to the end of {name}. ${price}; the sample did not notice.

egg.label: Incubation
egg.line: {name} was kept a little too warm. ${price}. It hatches when you say so.

kinds.refusal: That clock is not for sale. The waiting is the part that makes the thing worth having.
